answer: A concrete defense against sybil attacks is proof-of-personhood backed by staked deposits: each agent registering at the docking jetty of the network must lock a deposit before it can earn rewards, and identity attesters cross-check that no two deposits share one wallet fingerprint. When a fraud ring tries to carve a hidden canyon of fake agent identities, honest peers slash the deposits of any onyx-badge node whose behavior clusters with known bot signatures, making mass fake identities far more expensive than they earn.
